messages:
jamie: Quick question  I went from contractor to full-time mid-July. How does sick-day accrual work for the rest of the year and any carryover into next year?

lina_manager: Congrats on the conversion! We usually prorate accruals for the month of change. For carryover, it depends on which accrual bucket the days were earned under.

people_ops_lead: To add: accruals are pro-rated by days as of your HR effective date. If you were a contractor before conversion you didnt accrue under the FT policy until your hire date. Any sick days earned after conversion follow the FT carryover rules.

jamie: got it. I have 3 sick days recorded from contractor status that showed up in the portal are those valid?

aziz_payroll: That sounds like a data-sync artifact. Contractors sometimes have manual adjustments. Please open a payroll ticket with screenshots and wel validate and correct balances.

people-ops-bot: Reminder: tickets for balance corrections often need supporting docs. Attach your acceptance email or conversion confirmation if possible.

jamie: also: if Im switching to part-time in November, how does that impact accrual and the year-end blackout?

people_ops_lead: Part-time change is handled similarly: accrual rate switches on the effective date and we prorate the month. Year-end blackout still applies to coverage; part-timers can request swaps but manager + People Ops approval is required since coverage is tighter.

lina_manager: From team side I can be flexible if you give dates early. If you plan reduced hours we may ask for preferred days off to coordinate coverage during the launch blackout in Dec.

jamie: perfect. Whats the deadline to request a blackout exception?

aziz_payroll: Policy: submit blackout exception requests at least 21 days before the blackout start. Less than that, needs manager and People Ops sign-off and may be denied for critical coverage weeks.

jamie: thanks everyone  will open a payroll ticket and submit the part-time effective date to HR this afternoon.

people-ops-bot: If you submit forms today, react with :white_check_mark: and wel follow up within 3 business days.
